evidence.observation: Computes the next retention sweep at 18:00 Asia/Shanghai (10:00 UTC) and rolls to the following day when the current instant is already at/after that boundary. This is the scheduler clock for lifecycle transitions out of terminal project states.

The core retention state machine. It lists projects via wattclaw.team.project.list, filters by owned agents when provided, then for each project computes terminalStatus ('success'|'failed'|'fail'), terminalExpired (>= FINAL_PROJECT_RETENTION_MS = 3 days since updatedAt/createdAt), restoredExpired (status 'archived' with restoredAt >= RESTORED_PROJECT_RETENTION_MS = 24h), and archivedNeedsUnload (archived, restoredAt === 0, agents still loaded). Non-expired projects are 'skipped'/'kept'; expired projects are issued wattclaw.team.project.archive (except cold archived projects already unloaded, which are recorded without an RPC), and RPC failures land in 'failed'. Returns {scanned, kept, archived, skipped, failed}.

Activation/restore transition: lists gateway agents, re-creates only missing project members through wattclaw.team.project.member.update (replaying name/role/soul/skills/richSkills/models), refreshes agents.list if any member was restored, throws if any project agent id is still absent, and returns {project, agents, restored: status === 'archived'}. The 'restored' flag is how an archived project is marked as re-activated without rewriting its on-disk status.

Start precondition/state gate: after listing agents and detecting missing project agents, it applies the current gateway config (config.get -> config.apply) and polls agents.list until every project agent is loaded or timeoutMs elapses, otherwise throwing 'WattClaw agents were not loaded'. Used before a project run is allowed to progress into an active state.

Ownership projection executed on project updates: iterates project.members, registers each agent via trackAgent and the per-member main session key 'agent:<agentId>:main' via trackSession, returning {agentIds, sessionKeys}. This ties a user to the lifecycle of a project once its status advances.

Factory that owns the runtime event state: watchedProjects/clientProjects maps, subscribe/unsubscribe/stop/getActiveProjectCount. A watcher is created per project key ('<tenantId|single>:<projectId>') on first subscribe and closed when the last client unsubscribes, so client subscriptions drive the watcher lifecycle.

Maps filesystem state to project lifecycle events. For config.json it publishes 'wattclaw.team.project.updated' with payload.project, or 'wattclaw.team.project.deleted' when the file is missing (ENOENT); for task-list.json it publishes 'wattclaw.team.tasks.updated' with payload.tasks (or [] when missing) and rejects non-array content. Each accepted change increments entry.revision and de-duplicates identical raw content unless force=true (initial subscribe uses force).

Subscription transition: unsubscribes any prior project for the client, creates/reuses the watcher for the key, adds the client, then force-publishes the current config.json and task-list.json so a newly subscribed client immediately gets the current project status and tasks before subsequent debounced file-change events.

Resolves the on-disk project directory that the event watcher observes, validating tenantId/projectId path segments and probing container, host, gateway, /home/wattman/.openclaw and $HOME/.openclaw candidates; returns null when no candidate exists, which means no lifecycle events can be emitted for an unresolvable project.

claims.claim: Retention is the only transition that moves terminal projects to 'archived': pruneWattClawProjectsForUser archives projects whose status is success/failed/fail once >= 3 days have elapsed since updatedAt/createdAt, and archives already-'archived' projects once >= 24h have elapsed since restoredAt, while leaving non-terminal statuses (e.g. in_progress, pending) and fresh terminal projects untouched (kept).

Activation/restore is a distinct transition: activateWattClawProjectRuntime recreates missing project member agents with their original IDs and reports restored=true when the incoming project status is 'archived', so an archived project can become active again without the gateway file's status changing.
ensureWattClawProjectRuntime gates the start of a project on agent availability by applying gateway config and polling agents.list within a timeout, throwing when the project's agents never load.
The retention sweep is scheduled daily for 18:00 Asia/Shanghai by nextWattClawRetentionRunAt, which advances by 24h when the computed boundary has already passed.

Project status changes are observed as filesystem events: publishFile emits 'wattclaw.team.project.updated' when config.json changes and 'wattclaw.team.project.deleted' when config.json disappears, carrying projectId/tenantId/revision/project; task-list.json changes emit 'wattclaw.team.tasks.updated'.

Watcher lifetime is subscription-driven: createProjectWatcher starts an fs.watch on the project directory on the first subscribe, subscribe force-publishes current config and tasks to the new client, and unsubscribe closes the watcher once the last client leaves (getActiveProjectCount drops to 0).

state_transition_table.from: success | failed | fail (terminal, newer than 3 days)

state_transition_table.trigger: activate/start request with missing member agents
state_transition_table.to: active with restored=true (agents recreated via wattclaw.team.project.member.update; on-disk status stays archived)

state_transition_table.from: any status with missing project agents
state_transition_table.to: agents loaded (config.apply + poll) or error 'WattClaw agents were not loaded'
watched; immediate forced project.updated + tasks.updated events

conclusion: The WattClaw project lifecycle is split across two cooperating server modules. wattclaw-project-runtime.js drives authoritative state transitions over gateway RPC: projects move pending/planning/creating/waiting/in_progress -> success|failed (gateway-owned), and the runtime only transitions terminal projects (success/failed/fail) to 'archived' after a 3-day retention window, re-archives restored projects after 24 hours, and gates project start on agent availability via ensureWattClawProjectRuntime (config.apply + agents.list polling). Restoring an archived project is handled by activateWattClawProjectRuntime, which recreates only missing member agents and reports restored=true without rewriting the on-disk 'archived' status; server/index.js separately surfaces that SQLite restoredAt as a derived 'restored' status. wattclaw-project-events.js is the observability side of the same lifecycle: it resolves the per-tenant project directory, watches config.json and task-list.json, and publishes 'wattclaw.team.project.updated', 'wattclaw.team.project.deleted', and 'wattclaw.team.tasks.updated' (each carrying projectId, tenantId and a monotonic revision) over debounced, revision-deduplicated writes. Watch lifetime is subscription-driven: a watcher is created on first subscribe (with an immediate forced snapshot of config + tasks) and torn down when the last client unsubscribes, so event delivery and state-transition visibility are bounded by active client interest.

validation.command: node --input-type=module -e "...import both modules and assert retention transitions, activation restore, 18:00 Asia/Shanghai scheduling, and the events subscribe/updated/deleted/unsubscribe lifecycle..."
validation.notes: Ran a focused Node.js (v24.14.0) validation script against the two required modules: (1) nextWattClawRetentionRunAt maps 09:59Z and 10:00Z to 10:00Z and the following 10:00Z; (2) pruneWattClawProjectsForUser archived exactly the 3-day-old terminal project and the 24h-restored archived project, kept fresh-terminal/in_progress/pending/cold-archived projects, and issued no archive RPC for the cold archived project; (3) activateWattClawProjectRuntime recreated a missing member with its original ID and returned restored=true; (4) createWattClawProjectEventService emitted project.updated, tasks.updated, a status change to in_progress, and project.deleted on config.json removal, with getActiveProjectCount going 1 -> 0 after unsubscribe. All assertions passed. Limitation: the repository's declared test runner (vitest) is not installed in node_modules/.bin, and dependencies must not be installed, so the existing vitest suites (wattclaw-project-runtime.test.js, wattclaw-project-events.test.js) could not be executed; the equivalent checks above were run with Node's built-in assert instead.
